samples.summary: Durable documents attach on the ambient client first, then the whole editor is unmounted and re-attached, because `me` is undefined on the first render
samples.evidence: `useDurableDocument({ userId: me?.id === undefined ? undefined : String(me.id) })` (line 171-174). On the first render of any owned editor, `me` is `undefined` because the query key here is `['me','optional']` while every owned editor route primes `['me']` (document-detail.tsx:852, docs-detail.tsx:331, notes-detail.tsx:358, slides-detail.tsx:940, board-detail.tsx:241; only PublicRoute/shared-document/sheet-view use `['me','optional']`). With `me` undefined, `eligible` is false, `settled` is `!eligible` = true, so `inner` renders and the document attaches on the ambient client. When the query resolves, `eligible` flips true, `subject` changes, `answered` is false, so `settled` becomes false and line 199-201 `return null` unmounts the entire `DocumentProvider` subtree (detach + editor state destroyed), then re-mounts it under `DurableYorkieProvider`. That is precisely the 'attach the document twice on every durable open — and an edit made in that window would live in a client React is about to unmount' failure the comment at lines 188-198 claims is prevented. The new durable test suite mocks `useQuery` to return `me` synchronously, so it cannot see this.

samples.summary: A 401 session expiry erases the offline archives, destroying the only copy of work the SDK could not reconcile
samples.evidence: `logout()` now awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (auth.ts:105), which calls `store.dropAllForUser(who)`; `dropAllForUser` deletes live entries *and* `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:851). `logout()` is not only user-initiated: `fetchWithAuth` calls it on any 401 whose refresh failed (auth.ts:229). An archive is, by this feature's own design, the sole remaining copy of unsent edits the SDK gave up reconciling and which the recovery UI is supposed to hand back. So an expired session — a routine event, reachable from any background request — silently and irreversibly deletes that work before the user is ever offered it. The erase-on-sign-out intent does not cover an involuntary token expiry.

samples.summary: The per-document `WafflebaseDocStore` is never closed, leaking an open IndexedDB connection per document opened
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` with no cleanup effect calling `store.close()` on unmount. `WafflebaseDocStore` exposes `close()` precisely so `deleteDatabase`/version-change elsewhere is not blocked (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:403-408) and every other creator (offline-erase.ts:77, 107; offline-runtime.tsx cleanup) closes it. Navigating between documents in one session accumulates open `IDBDatabase` connections that survive until GC.

samples.summary: The fallback store created in `watchForOfflineDisable` is never closed
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` then `void eraseOfflineData(current, who).catch(...)` — when the fallback branch is taken (the documented Settings-route case, where no editor store exists) the connection it opens is never `close()`d, unlike `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` which closes in a `finally`.

samples.summary: Release-then-immediately-reacquire can be refused by the Web Locks manager, leaving the tab permanently non-durable with the lock free
samples.evidence: `release()` does `elections.delete(name); releaseLock();` (lines 183-184). `releaseLock()` only resolves the promise the lock callback is parked on; the browser frees the lock asynchronously. `acquireDurableSession` immediately afterwards issues `navigator.locks.request(name, { ifAvailable: true }, ...)` (webLocks(), line ~150 of this file), which resolves `undefined` if the name is still held at processing time. In `useDurableDocument` the release (effect cleanup) and the new acquire (new effect) are issued in the same commit, so this ordering is reachable on a docKey/userId change that returns to a previously held name. Nothing retries — the effect deps do not change again — so the tab reports non-durable for the rest of the document's life while the lock is actually free. This is the same failure class the in-tab reference counting was added to avoid, just across sequential mounts rather than StrictMode double-invocation.

samples.summary: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` clears the remembered user even when the sign-out does not complete, disabling later document purges for the rest of the session
samples.evidence: `const who = signedInUserId; signedInUserId = undefined;` runs unconditionally (lines 66-67). `logout()` awaits this *before* `if (res && !res.ok && !suppressFailure) throw new Error('Failed to log out')` (auth.ts:105-109), so a failed logout leaves the user signed in with `signedInUserId === undefined`. From then on `purgeOfflineDocuments` returns early (`if (!who ...) return`, line 96), so deleting a document no longer drops its local copy — the content stays on disk until the thirty-day sweep, which is the exact promise `deleteDocument`/`deleteDocuments` were changed to keep.

samples.summary: The recovery toasts outlive the component and use a store the cleanup has already closed
samples.evidence: The cleanup calls `store.close()` (line 90) while `offerRecoverableWork` may still be awaiting the network, and while the `duration: Infinity` toasts it already raised hold `store` in their `onClick`. Clicking 'Save a copy' after unmount calls `recoverOfflineCopy(store, ...)`, which re-opens the database (because `close()` clears `this.opening`) and leaves that new connection open with nobody to close it; the success handler then calls `navigate(...)` from an unmounted component. `cancelled` is not consulted inside the click handler.

samples.summary: `collectStale` is not scoped to the current user, unlike every other destructive path in the store
samples.evidence: `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` (line 873), `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 886) and `orphanSnapshotKeys()` (line 892) all span every user in the origin's database, while `dropAllForUser`, `listArchives`, `loadArchive`, `purgeDocument` and `evictOldest` are all carefully scoped by `userId`. On a shared device, one account's session sweep deletes another account's entries and — more seriously — another account's *archives*, which hold unreconciled work that account has never been offered, merely because that user did not sign in for thirty days.

samples.summary: Purging a deleted document's entry while it is still attached leaves the SDK silently appending into nothing
samples.evidence: `await purgeOfflineDocuments([id])` calls `store.purgeDocument` → `purge()`, which deletes the header without adding the key to `evicted`. If the document is open in this tab on a durable client (deleting from a document list while another view holds it, or deleting the open document), every later `appendChange` finds no header and returns the contract's silent success (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:540-542) instead of the loud `refuseIfEvicted` rejection the store uses for the analogous eviction case, so the SDK is never told its base is gone.

finding.summary: Durable documents attach on the ambient client first, then the whole editor is unmounted and re-attached, because `me` is undefined on the first render
finding.evidence: `useDurableDocument({ userId: me?.id === undefined ? undefined : String(me.id) })` (line 171-174). On the first render of any owned editor, `me` is `undefined` because the query key here is `['me','optional']` while every owned editor route primes `['me']` (document-detail.tsx:852, docs-detail.tsx:331, notes-detail.tsx:358, slides-detail.tsx:940, board-detail.tsx:241; only PublicRoute/shared-document/sheet-view use `['me','optional']`). With `me` undefined, `eligible` is false, `settled` is `!eligible` = true, so `inner` renders and the document attaches on the ambient client. When the query resolves, `eligible` flips true, `subject` changes, `answered` is false, so `settled` becomes false and line 199-201 `return null` unmounts the entire `DocumentProvider` subtree (detach + editor state destroyed), then re-mounts it under `DurableYorkieProvider`. That is precisely the 'attach the document twice on every durable open — and an edit made in that window would live in a client React is about to unmount' failure the comment at lines 188-198 claims is prevented. The new durable test suite mocks `useQuery` to return `me` synchronously, so it cannot see this.

verdict.reason: All factual claims check out. CollabDocumentProvider reads `['me','optional']` (collab-document-provider.tsx:165-169) while every owned editor route primes `['me']` (document-detail.tsx:852, docs-detail.tsx:331, notes-detail.tsx:358, slides-detail.tsx:940, board-detail.tsx:241), so `me` is undefined on the first render of an owned editor. With `userId` undefined, `eligible` is false (use-durable-document.ts:115-120) and `settled = !eligible || answered` is true (line 203), so `inner` renders and the document attaches on the ambient client. When the query resolves, `userId` changes, `subject` changes (line 135), `answered` is false (line 181), `eligible` is true, so `settled` flips false and collab-document-provider.tsx:199-201 returns null — unmounting the entire DocumentProvider subtree (detach + editor state destroyed) before remounting under DurableYorkieProvider. That is the exact attach-twice / edit-in-a-doomed-client failure the comment at lines 188-198 claims is prevented, and the durable suite cannot see it because it mocks useQuery to return `me` synchronously (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:70-72). The only mitigating fact is that `eligible` additionally requires supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:61-67), and the pin is 0.7.22 < MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (packages/frontend/package.json:65, vite.config.ts:360-364), so the durable branch is currently dark; but that is the feature's own build-time flag which the code documents as flipped by a dependency bump alone, not an independent guard, so it does not make the defect unreachable in any meaningful sense for this change.

finding.summary: A 401 session expiry erases the offline archives, destroying the only copy of work the SDK could not reconcile
finding.evidence: `logout()` now awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (auth.ts:105), which calls `store.dropAllForUser(who)`; `dropAllForUser` deletes live entries *and* `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:851). `logout()` is not only user-initiated: `fetchWithAuth` calls it on any 401 whose refresh failed (auth.ts:229). An archive is, by this feature's own design, the sole remaining copy of unsent edits the SDK gave up reconciling and which the recovery UI is supposed to hand back. So an expired session — a routine event, reachable from any background request — silently and irreversibly deletes that work before the user is ever offered it. The erase-on-sign-out intent does not cover an involuntary token expiry.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. auth.ts:105 unconditionally awaits eraseOfflineDataOnLogout() inside logout(); offline-erase.ts:65-79 resolves the remembered user and calls eraseOfflineData -> store.dropAllForUser (offline-erase.ts:30); wafflebase-doc-store.ts:842-853 purges live entries AND at :851 hard-deletes every archive row for that user via dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...) (:973-988), with no archive-sparing branch. logout() is reachable involuntarily: fetchWithAuth's 401 arm (auth.ts:221-236) calls logout({redirect:false, showSuccessToast:false, suppressFailure:true}) whenever a refresh fails, on any authenticated request (fetchMe, fetchYorkieToken, document APIs). The identity required for the erase is present on that path because OfflineRuntime (offline-runtime.tsx:42, mounted by PrivateRoute) records it, and offline-erase.ts:42-44 explicitly states module state is used so the fetchWithAuth 401 arm can run it. Archives are the sole remaining copy of work the SDK gave up reconciling and are designed to outlive a session — the recovery offer drops an archive only after the copy is written (offline-copy-recovery.ts:152-186), and the feature's own spec states "a declined offer survives to the next session" (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:197-201). A routine token expiry therefore silently and irreversibly deletes unrecovered work before the user is offered it. No option exists on logout() to skip the erase, and the 401 call site passes none; the swallow-on-failure in eraseOfflineDataOnLogout does not prevent a successful erase. Real data-loss bug on a normally reachable path — critical under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: `LossWatch` calls `useDocument()` above the `DocumentProvider`, so the loss latch can never be set (or the render throws)
finding.evidence: In `DurableYorkieProvider` the tree is `KeyedYorkieProvider > LockRefusalWatch > LossWatch > {children}`, and `children` is `inner` from collab-document-provider.tsx:163-168 — which *is* the `DocumentProvider`. So `LossWatch`'s `useDocument()` (line 122) runs outside any `DocumentProvider`. Either the hook throws (crashing every durable document) or `doc` is undefined, the `useEffect` returns early (line 125), and `store.expectLoss(...)` is never called. Without the latch, `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` treats every removal as an ordinary detach and deletes the entry instead of archiving it — the unsent work the whole offline-copy path exists to hand back is silently destroyed. The durable test suite mocks `@yorkie-js/react`'s `useDocument` to always return a doc (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:31-40), so it cannot detect this.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `DurableYorkieProvider` renders `KeyedYorkieProvider > LockRefusalWatch > DurableDocumentScope > {children}` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:111-125); there is no loss-watch component in that tree, and line 122 is the `</LockRefusalWatch>` close tag, not a `useDocument()` call. The loss watch is a separate exported component, `DurableLossWatch` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:149-167), which reads the store from React context via `useDurableDocumentContext()` rather than from props, and it is mounted at collab-document-provider.tsx:183 INSIDE the `<DocumentProvider>` opened at line 177 — so its `useDocument()` call is under the provider it needs, while `DurableDocumentScope` (line 121) wrapping `inner` (line 224) supplies the store. A repo-wide grep for `LossWatch` yields only the definition and that single import/usage, so there is no alternate mount site above a `DocumentProvider`. `useDurableDocumentContext()` returns `undefined` instead of throwing outside a durable client (durable-document-context.ts:56-58), making the unconditional render a safe no-op for non-durable documents. The `expectLoss` latch path (lines 160-162) is therefore reachable, and the claimed crash/silent-data-destruction premise does not exist in this tree.

finding.summary: Share links are NOT structurally excluded: a signed-in visitor gets a durable client with the wrong auth token
finding.evidence: The docstring at lines 137-140 asserts "`shared-document.tsx` mounts its own provider, so anonymous share links are excluded structurally". They are not: shared-document.tsx:979-1042 renders `CollabDocumentProvider` inside its share-token `YorkieProvider`. For a *signed-in* visitor on someone else's share link, `me` is defined, `isExcluded` (use-durable-document.ts:31) only refuses `pdf-` keys, so with the preference on the durable path mounts a nested `DurableYorkieProvider` with `authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:198) instead of `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (shared-document.tsx:976). The attach then carries the user's own credential, which they may not have for that document — the share view breaks — and the share document is persisted to disk under `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` regardless.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that no positional exclusion exists for share links — is false in this repository. `use-durable-document.ts:43-69` defines a `DurabilityPermitted` context plus an exported `NonDurableScope`, and it is consumed in the eligibility conjunction at `use-durable-document.ts:110` and `:115-120` (`supportsClientKey() && permitted && enabled && ...`). `shared-document.tsx:982` wraps the share-token `YorkieProvider` and all five `CollabDocumentProvider` branches (`:991-1056`) in `<NonDurableScope>`, closing at `:1058`, so `permitted` is false for every share-link document; `durable` is false (`:182`) and `clientKey` undefined (`:198`), and `collab-document-provider.tsx:203` returns the ambient path, never reaching the `DurableYorkieProvider` with `authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken}` at `:208-216`. The docstring the finding quotes ("shared-document.tsx mounts its own provider, so anonymous share links are excluded structurally") does not exist; `collab-document-provider.tsx:140-145` states the opposite and points at the `NonDurableScope` wrapper. The one share branch rendered outside that wrapper, `SharedPdfLayout` (`shared-document.tsx:718-758`), uses docKey `pdf-${documentId}` (`app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:200`) and is caught by `isExcluded` (`use-durable-document.ts:39-41`). No signed-in-visitor path reaches the durable branch on a share link.

finding.summary: Quota eviction selects victims across all users, deleting another account's unsent work on a shared device
finding.evidence: `evictOldest` builds candidates from `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, IDBKeyRange.lowerBound(-Infinity))` (lines 981-984), which is the `updatedAt` index over *every* header row in the origin database, with no `userId` filter. The rest of the class is scrupulous about scoping (`dropAllForUser` filters by `BY_USER`, `listArchives`/`loadArchive` refuse other users' rows), and the class docstring for `dropAllForUser` says signing out of one account "must not destroy another's unsent work" — but a single quota-pressured `saveSnapshot` by user A will `purge` user B's oldest entry, unsent log included. `collectStale`'s `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 839) is likewise unscoped.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present as described. `evictOldest` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1027-1057) first builds `mine = headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, IDBKeyRange.only(this.userId))` (:1034-1036) and then, while walking the `BY_UPDATED_AT` candidate list, skips any key not in that set (`if (!mine.has(docKey)) continue;` :1043) before also skipping the key being written (:1044) and live docs (:1045). The `updatedAt` index is used purely for ordering, so a quota-pressured saveSnapshot by user A cannot purge user B's row. The lines the finding quotes as evictOldest's unscoped query (981-984) actually belong to `dropArchivesWhere` (:973-988), and the line it cites for collectStale (839) is inside `dropAllForUser`'s user-scoped archive drop (:851). The secondary point about `collectStale` (real unscoped calls at :873 and :886) is the documented age-based retention sweep (docstring :855-863, DefaultMaxAgeMs 30 days at :141, live rows spared via isLive at :876); it deletes only rows past the retention cutoff — the same outcome the owner's own sweep would produce — and is not the claimed "quota eviction deletes another account's unsent work" mechanism.

finding.summary: `durable` is never passed to `deriveSyncState`, so `saved-locally` is unreachable and durable documents still report "Not saved"
finding.evidence: `deriveSyncState` gained a `durable` signal (sync-state.ts:70,85) and the chip gained a `saved-locally` label/icon/tooltip, but the only production caller is `use-sync-status.ts:214`, which passes `{ connected, pending, syncFailed }` and nothing else, so `durable` always defaults to `false`. The new state is dead in the app: a document whose unsent edits are on disk still shows the destructive "Not saved" chip. This also breaks the invariant the PDF exclusion is justified by in use-durable-document.ts:26-29 ("whatever is durable must be reportable").

verdict.reason: The absence claim is factually wrong at the cited file. use-sync-status.ts:220 calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed, durable })` — `durable` IS passed. The reviewer cited line 214, which is `hasUnsentEdits: unflushed,` inside the separate `if (!doc)` early-return block (lines 210-217) that hardcodes `state: 'saved'` and never invokes deriveSyncState; they inspected the wrong object literal. The signal is real end-to-end, not a stub: use-sync-status.ts:75 binds `const durable = useDocumentDurability()` (imported at line 3); durable-document-context.ts:67-69 implements it as `useContext(DurableDocumentContext)?.durable ?? false`, defaulting false only outside a durable client; and durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:106-109,121 publishes `{ store, durable: !lost, reportLoss }` via `<DurableDocumentScope>`, so durable is genuinely true while a durable client is mounted and no loss has latched. Therefore sync-state.ts:85 (`return durable ? 'saved-locally' : 'not-saved'`) is reachable in production, `saved-locally` is not dead, durable documents do not show the destructive "Not saved" chip, and the dependent claim about the use-durable-document.ts invariant collapses with its premise.

finding.summary: `watchForOfflineDisable` and `collectStale` are never invoked from application code, so the "turning this off deletes them" promise and the 30-day sweep never run
finding.evidence: A grep for `watchForOfflineDisable`, `collectStale`, `eraseOfflineData`, `listRecoverableWork`, `recoverOfflineCopy` and `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` finds matches only inside `src/lib/*.test.*` and the modules themselves — no route, no Settings page, no app bootstrap. So nothing ever sets the preference, nothing installs the disable watcher, and nothing schedules stale collection. The store's own comments call an uncollected archive store "a quota leak that looks like a feature" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:837-838) and offline-erase.ts:13 quotes Settings copy that does not exist yet. If the preference is ever flipped by hand (localStorage), documents accumulate forever with no collection and no erase.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false; multiple production (non-test) call sites exist. `OfflineRuntime` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx) imports and calls `watchForOfflineDisable` at :56 and `await store.collectStale()` at :69 (default maxAgeMs is the 30-day sweep per wafflebase-doc-store.ts:856,864), and calls `listRecoverableWork` at :111 and `recoverOfflineCopy` at :138. This component is not dead code: PrivateRoute.tsx:7 imports it and :35 renders it for every authenticated session, and PrivateRoute is a live route element at App.tsx:128. The Settings page the finding says does not exist is at packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx, which imports `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` at :21 and binds it to the offline Switch at :111-115, with the exact quoted copy "turning it off deletes what was stored" at :108. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` is called from production code at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:105 (imported :4). Therefore the preference is set from the UI, the disable watcher is installed at session start, and stale collection is scheduled once per session — the promised behaviors all have wiring.

finding.summary: `remove()` consumes the loss latch before the transaction commits and is not wrapped in `atomically`
finding.evidence: `remove()` (lines 663-706) deletes the latch with `this.expectedLosses.delete(documentKeyOf(docKey))` at line 681, then issues the archive `put` and three deletes, then awaits `completed(tx)` at line 704. Unlike `saveSnapshot`/`appendChange`/`saveMeta`, it does not use `WafflebaseDocStore.atomically`, so (a) if the archive `put` or any delete throws synchronously mid-sequence, the already-issued requests still commit — e.g. the snapshot deleted while the archive put never happened, which destroys the only copy of the unsent work; and (b) if the transaction aborts (quota is plausible here, since archiving doubles the entry's footprint and `remove` has no `withQuotaRetry`), the latch has already been consumed, so a retried removal will take the ordinary-detach path and delete without archiving.

verdict.reason: The code does not exist as described. `remove()` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:663-722) wraps the archive `put` and all three deletes inside `await WafflebaseDocStore.atomically(tx, ...)` at line 684 (body 685-718), and it only *reads* the latch before the transaction (`const losing = this.expectedLosses.has(documentKey)` at line 677, with an explanatory comment at 670-675 naming this very hazard). The consuming `this.expectedLosses.delete(documentKey)` sits at line 720, AFTER the awaited `atomically` resolves — which only happens once `completed(tx)` (line 1077) fires `oncomplete` (line 1092). If the body throws, `atomically`'s catch (1079-1086) calls `tx.abort()` and rethrows, so the already-issued deletes do not commit; if the transaction aborts (quota included), `completed` rejects (1093-1094) and line 720 never runs, so the latch survives and a retried removal still archives. Both halves (a) and (b) of the finding are false against this tree; the reviewer's cited line numbers (latch delete at 681, `completed(tx)` at 704) point at a comment and at archive-record construction respectively. The one true residual detail — `remove` has no `withQuotaRetry` — carries none of the claimed harm, since the latch is not consumed on abort. docs/tasks/active/20260917-wafflebase-doc-store-todo.md:219-224 records these two exact problems as already fixed with covering tests, matching what the code now shows.
